## Load Libraries and Data

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(readODS)
library(tidyverse)
library(waffle)
library(gridExtra)
library(stringr)

data <- read_ods("C:/Users/clint/OneDrive/Code/Python/2025 30DCC Python/04 big or small/Day 04_big_or_small.ods")

head(data)

data <- data |> 
  filter(org != "Wild (20-100 chimps)")
```

## Produce Waffle Chart

```{r}
# Create the data frame
data <- data.frame(
  org = factor(c("ZAA Cage", "AZA Cage", "Wild and Free"),
               levels = c("ZAA Cage", "AZA Cage", "Wild and Free")),
  value = c(1, 8, 355),  # Changed from 241 to 341
  color = c("#38040E", "#D5A021", "darkgreen") 
)

# Expand the data frame
expanded_data <- data.frame(
  org = factor(unlist(sapply(1:nrow(data), function(i) rep(as.character(data$org[i]), data$value[i]))), 
               levels = as.character(data$org)),
  color = unlist(sapply(1:nrow(data), function(i) rep(data$color[i], data$value[i])))
)

# Calculate row and column positions
rows <- 14  # Increased from 10 to 14 rows to accommodate more squares without expanding area
n_cols <- ceiling(nrow(expanded_data) / rows)
expanded_data$index <- 1:nrow(expanded_data)
expanded_data$col <- ((expanded_data$index - 1) %% n_cols) + 1
expanded_data$row <- rows - floor((expanded_data$index - 1) / n_cols)

# Define the subtitle text
subtitle_text <- "The Zoological Association of America (ZAA) only requires 240 square feet of space for an adult chimp, while the American Association of Zoos and Aquariums requires 2,000. In the wild, chimps have more than 3,000,000 square feet of space with their community. This plot doesn't have enough space to show how massive the chimp territory in the wild truly is."

# Define the caption text - using a consistent width for wrapping
caption_text <- "Data Sources: King, B.J. Animals' Best Friends: Putting Compassion to Work for Animals in Captivity and in the Wild (2021) and Fultz et al. How Sanctuary Chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes) Use Space after Being Introduced to a Large Outdoor Habitat. Animals (Basel). 2023 Mar 7;13(6):961."

# Create the waffle plot
p <- ggplot(expanded_data, aes(x = col, y = row, fill = org)) +
  geom_tile(color = "gray90", linewidth = 0.8) +  # Slightly thinner lines to accommodate more squares
  scale_fill_manual(name = NULL, values = setNames(data$color, as.character(data$org))) +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title = "The Space Divide: Minimum Chimp Habitat in Zoos and the Wild",
    subtitle = str_wrap(subtitle_text, width = 80),
    caption = str_wrap(caption_text, width = 80)
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0, margin = margin(b = 10), size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0, margin = margin(b = 15), size = 12, face = "italic"),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 8, margin = margin(t = 15)),
    plot.margin = margin(l = 20, r = 20, t = 20, b = 20),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90", color = NA)
  )

# Ensure the plot has enough space for all text elements
p <- p + theme(aspect.ratio = 0.8)

# Print the plot
print(p)

# Save the plot with the specified dimensions
ggsave("Day 04_big_or_small.png", plot = p, width = 8, height = 7, units = "in")
```
